Rank measures your training and power — it sets your ability score point budget, how many power sets/powers/traits you can pick, and it also equals your starting Karma.
Origin explains how your hero got their powers — it automatically grants a package of traits and tags tied to that origin (for example, Mutant, Weird Science, or Magic).
Occupation is your hero's civilian job or role — it grants its own package of traits and tags on top of the ones from your Origin, reflecting the skills of that career.

Background

📊 Rank Builds
Rank Builds is an optional tool (not part of the official rules): snapshot each rank's build under one character as you play from civilian to hero. Flip the toggle to enable it.
🎓 How Rank Builds Work
1. Enable it & start at your lowest rank — Flip the toggle above (Rank Builds is optional — not part of the official rules), then build your character the way they are when play begins. Lots of Narrators start heroes as Rank 1 civilians.
2. Snapshot the build — Tap 📸 Save current build. That rank's full build (stats, powers, traits, tags, gear) is filed under this one character — no more separate vault entries per rank.
3. Play & advance — Track advancement with 🎓 Getting Schooled (Play → Reference), or use the ⬆ Rank Up button below.
4. Auto-save on rank-up — Ranking up automatically snapshots the rank you're leaving (unless you already saved it), so a build is never lost by accident.
5. Flip between ranks — Tap a rank chip or 📂 Load to bring back any past build — handy for flashback sessions or remembering what you used to look like.
6. Everything travels together — Snapshots are stored inside the character, so they save, load, and restore from the trash right along with it. Photos stay on the current build; snapshots keep the stats.

Speed

spaces  ·  1 space = 5 ft.  ·  Combat / Out of Combat
Speed sets how far you move on a movement action. Run Speed starts at 5 spaces, +1 for every full 5 points of Agility (and ±1 for Big/Small size); Climb, Jump, and Swim Speed are each half your Run Speed.

              Powers & Traits

              Powers, traits, tags & narrative powers

              ⭐ Points & Resources

              Karma and Sinister Plot Points are unlocked by the Heroic or Villainous tags. Add one of those tags in the Traits section to activate your resource pool.
              Add the Heroic tag to activate
              Karma is earned through heroic deeds and spent to improve abilities or re-roll dice. Starting Karma = Rank.
              Add the Villainous tag to activate
              Sinister Plot Points fuel villainous schemes and power boosts. Starting SPP = Rank.

              Powers (0/4)

              Powers are your hero's active superhuman abilities — many belong to a themed Power Set, while some (basic powers) stand alone. Your Rank determines how many you can take.

                Traits (0)

                Traits have a real mechanical effect — bonuses, special rules, and sometimes drawbacks that can earn you Karma when they come up in play. Your Rank sets how many extra traits you can pick beyond what your Origin and Occupation already grant.

                  Stunts (0)
                  Stunts are tricks learned through experience with a power or piece of equipment. The Narrator awards a stunt after a Fantastic success using its prerequisite in an adventure (or intensive training) — record it here once learned. Under the X-Men "Getting Schooled" rules, a stunt can be picked instead of ticking off a schooling box.
                  Stunts cost no picks. Unless stated otherwise, only one stunt special effect applies per Fantastic success.
                  Available Stunts

                  Tags(0 manual)

                  Tags are narrative labels with no mechanical effect — things like Secret Identity or Public Identity. They just describe your character's story. You can have as many as you like.

                        ⚔ Active Combat

                        📖 Combat Actions (Spider-Verse & Avengers Expansions)
                        🗡 Disarm — standard action (Spider-Verse p.135 / Avengers p.155)
                        Melee or Agility attack with trouble against an object/weapon held by someone else. Already grabbed the target? Ignore the trouble. Disarming someone another character grabbed? Trouble stacks with the entangled-attack rules.
                        Success: target drops it in an adjacent space. Fantastic: it's destroyed (iconic weapons can't be). Fantastic with melee: may take it instead (if not attached). Picking up/readying a dropped item takes an action.
                        Only common handheld or improvised weapons — never mounted or physically attached weapons.
                        With webbing: Webcasting → Agility attack with trouble; success webs the weapon to something solid; Fantastic yanks it from their hand (take or hurl away). Webgrabbing → Agility attack with trouble; success grabs the weapon; Fantastic gums it up, disabled 1 hour. After any such success, a standard action or reaction makes a Melee vs. target's Melee defense check — success yanks the weapon away; Fantastic leaves them surprised for one round.
                        🔧 Gadget Hacking — (Avengers p.145)
                        Build a gadget to neutralize a foe's powers. Requires prior observation/inspiration, materials, and time.
                        Build: Logic vs. TN 13 to neutralize one power; each additional power raises TN by +1. Lab Access grants an edge; having built that gadget before grants another edge.
                        Success: creates a one-use gadget. Fantastic: also grants an edge when rebuilding it.
                        Deploy: requires a successful Melee or Agility attack; a missed Agility attack destroys the gadget. Successful use neutralizes the chosen powers for the remainder of combat. Gadget has 10 Health.
                        Only Rich characters can retain permanent gadgets beyond an adventure; others may use a Patron.
                        😤 Taunt — reaction (p.114)
                        Goad an enemy and make a Vigilance check.
                        Success: the taunted character must target the taunting character with their next attack.
                        Fantastic success: they also have trouble on that attack.
                        ★ Ultimate Fantastic Initiative (p.135)
                        A 6 M 6 on an initiative check is an ultimate Fantastic success: the character takes part in the bonus round and may turn their Marvel die to an M on any single action check during it. Mark it with the 6M6? toggle on the initiative screen.

                        🗡 Team Maneuvers

                        Heroes (or villains) on the same team can use one special group maneuver per battle. Pick a type at the start of the adventure. Activate only at the start of a round. Each participant must be within 5 spaces of another participant, able to communicate, and pay Focus (or 1 Karma).
                        Browse & Filter Maneuvers
                        Rules reminder
                        • Team = at least 2 characters. No upper limit.
                        • A character on multiple teams may only join one team maneuver per battle.
                        • Outsiders don’t benefit unless they declare a team-up for the adventure.
                        • Choose type at adventure start; switch only once per day (at HQ / safe strategy talk).
                        • Lower level of the same type is always allowed (pay the lower cost).
                        • Unconscious/demoralized members need not join; if they can pay, they may still benefit.
                        • Villain teams can use these too.
                        • Focus costs scale with level — edit defaults in the panel if your table differs.

                        ☄️ Secret Wars Rules Reference

                        Infections, desperate measures, henchmen, resize clarifications, and starship rules — Secret Wars Expansion.
                        🩸 Self-Sacrifice — (p.164)
                        A hero out of Focus to spend who is (or would become) demoralized may declare self-sacrifice.
                        Effect: no longer demoralized until the battle ends; the Focus-spend cap is lifted; may spend Focus below 0, down to shattered but not past it. Each Focus spent after the declaration costs 1 Health, applied at the end of the battle (ignoring Damage Reduction and Elemental Protection).
                        If not killed, the hero must make an Absurd Resilience check: fail = killed anyhow; success = Health falls to 0 and they fall unconscious.
                        👥 Henchmen — (p.154)
                        Fast Narrator-built mooks, weaker than their boss. Usually Rank 1–2 (Rank 3 at most, for high-rank villains); always a lower rank than their boss.
                        Ability scores total up to 5 × rank (simplest: each = rank, except one — often Logic — at 0). One trait per rank; one power per rank (respecting prerequisites). Apply tags that fit the concept; otherwise skip tags.
                        🧟 Hunger Virus — (p.164)
                        Bite/scratch + at least 1 damage → immediate Resilience vs. TN 25 (no action). Fantastic: immune for 1 day. Success: protected from that bite only. Fail: infected — the virus incubates almost instantly and deals dMarvel ×3 Health damage per round, ignoring Health Damage Reduction.
                        Healing powers can stave it off but cannot cure it — the Cure-All power does not affect it at all. Resurrect revives a zombie only temporarily.
                        🪚 Amputation — (p.165)
                        If the infecting bite was not a Fantastic success, roll 1d6: 1 = left leg, 2 = right leg, 3–4 = left arm, 5–6 = right arm.
                        Amputate within 12 rounds: a helper attacks the infected character and needs a Fantastic success. TN drops to 10 if the victim holds still; Damage Reduction still applies; self-amputation has trouble. The attack must deal at least half the infected part's full Health. Success ends the infection. Narrator decides lasting effects (e.g. Mobility Issues).
                        🧟‍♂️ Undead Life — (p.165)
                        A victim who dies from the Hunger transforms into a zombie that hungers for living flesh. Their Health returns to full and they gain the Monstrous: Marvel Zombie origin.
                        🐺 Lycanthropy — (p.166)
                        Bite/scratch + at least 1 damage → immediate Resilience vs. TN 25. Fantastic: immune for 1 day. Fail: fully cursed dMarvel hours later (a Marvel result = end of combat). Those aware of their condition can transform willingly.
                        No known cure — Cure-All does not affect it. The victim gains the Monstrous: Werewolf origin (plus the Extraordinary Origin trait for free if they already had an origin).
                        🕷️ Spider-Virus — (p.166)
                        Bite/scratch + at least 1 damage from anything carrying it (even a bedbug). Characters with an origin other than Special Training are immune. Immediate Resilience vs. TN 25 (Fantastic = 1-day immunity; success = protected from that bite). Fail: gains the Weird Science origin (+2 ranks; Mighty 1, Jump 1, Spider-Sense, Wallcrawling, Webcasting, Webslinging; +2 Resilience & Vigilance, +3 Melee & Agility).
                        Then Resilience vs. TN 12 under great stress or a Spider-Queen mental attack: fail = third stage (giant spider form: Additional Limbs + Enhanced Senses 1, loses other powers, bound to the Spider-Queen's hive mind). Airborne within 2 spaces; on Spider-Island it affects the super-powered too (immune: Spider-Powers, symbiotes, synthetics).
                        📐 Resize Clarifications — (p.195)
                        Flight: most speeds are recalculated when size changes, but Flight Speed does not change — the character flies at their regular Flight Speed no matter their size.
                        Growing Into Spaces: little-or-smaller occupants stay put (they can share the space). Average-or-larger characters are shoved to the fewest adjacent spaces possible. If what they push against is unmovable, the growing character moves their own center instead. Crushing someone = throwing yourself at them: Agility vs. their Agility defense; failure damages the attacker, success damages both.
                        🚀 Starship Rules — (pp.182–184)
                        Starships as HQs: large starships work like regular vehicles but are big enough to serve as mobile headquarters — use headquarters traits and tags, plus the starship-specific ones below.
                        Faster-Than-Light Travel: Exo-Space (Hyperspace/Subspace — leave reality, re-enter elsewhere; tricky to navigate) · Wormholes (tunnels between two fixed points; natural ones last anywhere from eons to moments) · Teleportation (instant; portals work like wormholes) · Stargates (devices creating wormholes between two points; galactic empires network them).
                        Starship Battles: work like vehicle battles, but the stakes are higher — a disabled starship in space may mean everyone inside dies. A ship that stops working loses shields but keeps its momentum (speed + direction); it maintains life support unless destroyed.
                        Getting Spaced: destroyed ship = no life support; occupants without Environmental Protection take dMarvel Health/round from asphyxiation (DR doesn't apply).
                        Moving in Zero-G: characters who can fly or swingline move normally. Otherwise they can't change direction unless they push off something — they float in a straight line at their last speed. Grabbable surfaces = use Climb Speed; a single push-off point = Jump Speed.
                        Explosive Decompression: Fantastic-success damage punctures the hull — everyone in the holed compartment has trouble on all actions for 1 round, then auto-repairs seal it.
                        Boarding: smash in with a damaging Fantastic attack (hole seals in 1 round), or attach boarding equipment (both ships within 10 spaces and stationary; Agility vs. TN 10 if resisted, must deal ≥1 damage).
                        Teleporting: shields block it. Treat the operator as having Teleport 2 + Teleport Other + Teleport Blind.
                        Starship Size (Team Rank 1–6): Average/Big/Huge/Gigantic/Titanic/Gargantuan — passengers 1/2/5/20/80/320 — Health 100/200/300/400/600/1000. Flight 36 with a star drive, 24 without. Cozy tag drops one size; Roomy bumps up one size. Ships can squeeze double passenger capacity.
                        📦 Narrative Items — (pp.170–173) Narrator-controlled; work as described, not as regular items/powers.
                        🧊 Cosmic Cube — (p.170)
                        A containment unit filled with energy drained from the all-powerful Beyonders. The energy is sentient and can fulfill the wishes of the person who holds and commands it. The sentience interprets and fulfills the user's will as best it can — but it can misunderstand, so the user must literally be careful what they wish for.
                        A Cosmic Cube can be used to change reality, but it cannot affect the past or alter a person's soul. It can edit memories or create a new version of a person to make them think the past was different, but the original person's soul and the original timeline remain intact.
                        🛡️ Celestial Armor — (p.170)
                        A gigantic battle suit that serves not to give the wearer power but to help control and contain them. Celestials are beings of energy from outside the Multiverse; their armor lets them exist within reality and interact with it while keeping them and their surroundings relatively safe.
                        Inside: mechanical and electronic systems plus automated defenses. Celestials rarely die, but leave their armor behind — it can be repurposed (Avengers Mountain was originally the armor of the Celestial Progenitor).
                        🏭 Elemental Converter — (p.170)
                        Galactus keeps this massive device stored on the Taa II. It transforms a planet's energy into a form easier for Galactus to consume — a food processor on a planetary scale. Takes roughly 24 hours to assemble (half that in a rush).
                        Galactus usually protects it, but if drawn away or distracted, the Converter can be dismantled or destroyed — only a temporary reprieve, as he can rebuild it.
                        🎭 Eternity Mask — (p.171)
                        Fashioned from a bit of the fabric of the universe. Anyone who wears it has their powers increased to make them an equal match to any foe they face — but it does not reduce the wearer's existing powers, abilities, Health, or Focus.
                        Grants the wearer all the powers of any foe they face, boosts ability scores and Health/Focus to the foe's numbers, and grants the Intuition power. Wearing it does not guarantee victory — only an equal footing. It does not work when the user intends to commit evil acts.
                        👑 Galactus' Armor — (p.171)
                        Like Celestial armor, designed to help Galactus contain and control the incredible power he wields. He can survive without it, but interacting with matter without destroying it is harder.
                        If he removes his helmet, he remains solid; if he removes the whole suit, he transforms back into his natural state: a humanoid form of pure energy.
                        💎 Infinity Stones — (pp.171–172)
                        From the First Cosmos; each works fully only in its home universe (elsewhere they function but may shatter if pushed). Currently: Power (Violet), Mind (Yellow), Reality (Red), Soul (Orange), Space (Blue), Time (Green), Death (Black).
                        Each grants its listed powers plus unlimited Focus (spend up to 30 at once for narrative purposes). A single stone grants +1 rank; each stone within 100 spaces of another grants +1 rank to all the stones' users (max Rank 6).
                        Death: knows the location of everyone about to die; teleport anywhere; escort the dead; instantly kill with a touch (cannot spare the dying). Mind: all Telekinesis + Telepathy powers (no prereqs); travel through dreams; construct psychic weapons; Brilliance 4, Uncanny 4. Power: all Elemental Control (all types), Power Control, Super-Strength powers (no prereqs); Mighty 4, Sturdy 4. Reality: alter physical reality; change size/density/composition; all Elemental Control (all types), Luck, Phasing, Resize, Teleportation (no prereqs); Flight 2, Mighty 4, Sturdy 4. Soul: examine/reach into souls to damage, heal, or alter; all Healing + Telepathy (no prereqs); conjure soul-based constructs; Discipline 4, Uncanny 4. Space: travel in space; control positions of things; teleport anything any size over unlimited distances; all Teleportation (no prereqs). Time: slow, speed up, freeze time; age or youthen people/things; see past and future; all Omniversal Travel (Time) + Sixth Sense (no prereqs).
                        🧤 Infinity Gauntlet — (p.172)
                        When the Infinity Stones are gathered together and controlled by a single person, they grant unlimited power and the user becomes Rank X. A right-handed golden glove with a slot per finger plus one on the back of the hand.
                        Makes its user one of the most powerful beings in the universe — only Eternity, Infinity, the Living Tribunal, and the One Above All can counter it. The user is effectively omnipotent: remake all reality in their universe at will. The only limits are their imagination and, perhaps, their arrogance.
                        ⚛️ ISO-8 — (p.172)
                        Also known as neutronium. A material usually found in Exo-Space — the pure creative force from which reality is created. Earth-15513 (the universe that held Battleworld) had large amounts; the Elders of the Universe fought over it, assembling it into an ISO-Sphere.
                        In game terms, each shard grants a user a pool of 100 Focus points to use at will, without normal rank-based limitations. Once consumed, the shard vanishes.
                        🔮 ISO-Sphere — (pp.172–173)
                        Uses Celestial technology to collect and control ISO-8. Fills like a ball of glass with liquid; when complete, forms a transparent, spiked casing hovering near its controller. Takes 1,000 ISO-8 shards to fill — nearly impossible under most circumstances.
                        Functions much like a Cosmic Cube, limited only by its user's imagination. If two people struggle for control, the one with the stronger desire becomes its controller.
                        💜 M'kraan Crystal — (p.173)
                        A purple crystal the size of a truck, on a planet near the galaxy's center, guarded by Jahf and Modt. Serves as the Nexus of All Realities — those who enter can travel to any other universe in the Multiverse or to the Panoptichron; even a shard grants this to its holder.
                        Supposedly houses the White Hot Room. Said to exist in all universes simultaneously — destroying it could wipe out the Multiverse.
                        🚪 Siege Courageous — (p.173)
                        A door-sized portal the controller can use to teleport to any other place on the same planet. The user must know the intended destination but need not have been there before. When activated, a similar portal opens in the new location; it remains open on both sides until deactivated, and can be deactivated from either side.
                        ☄️ Ultimate Nullifier — (p.173)
                        A pistol-sized weapon that can theoretically destroy the universe. When fired, it eliminates whatever target the user wishes — but if the user's mind isn't powerful enough, it eliminates them as well. A Rank X user could fire it without dying and even make it so the target never existed.
                        Galactus normally keeps it on his starship, the Taa II, and can recall it at will. (See The Cataclysm of Kang for more on this weapon.)

                        Headquarters & Vehicles

                        Build a team base & fleet — traits, tags, roster, downtime & vehicles

                        🎓 How to Build a Headquarters
                        1. Identity — Give your HQ a name and a short description. This is flavor — make it yours.
                        2. Team Roster & Rank — Add your team members and set the team's average rank. Rank determines how many traits you get (3 per rank).
                        3. Tags — Pick narrative tags that describe the HQ. Cozy vs Roomy, Mobile vs Stationary — these shape what the place feels like.
                        4. Traits — Choose traits like Armory, Medical Bay, or Security Measures. You get 3 per team rank. Some can be taken multiple times for stronger effects.
                        5. Downtime — Each trait unlocks downtime activities your heroes can do between missions.
                        6. Damage & Repair — Track the HQ's Health here. When it takes damage in play, mark it off and repair it during downtime.
                        7. Or start from a Profile — Don't want to build from scratch? Pick a Headquarters Profile (Avengers Tower, X-Mansion, etc.) to auto-fill tags and traits.
                        8. Save — Hit save in the Saved Headquarters section to keep it. You can build multiple HQs and switch between them.

                        🚀 Starship Builder (Secret Wars)

                        🎓 How to Build a Starship
                        1. Pick Team Rank — Choose your team's average rank (1–6). The book's Starship Size table automatically fills in Size, Health, and Passengers.
                        2. Size Adjustment — Cozy drops one size (adds the Cozy tag); Roomy bumps up one size (adds the Roomy tag). Or leave it Normal.
                        3. FTL Travel — Pick how the ship travels faster than light (Wormholes, Teleportation, Stargates, etc.), or leave it blank for sublight only.
                        4. Add Traits — Click trait buttons to quick-add them. Star Drive boosts Flight Speed to 36. Shields, Mines, and Plasma Cannons can be taken up to 4 times each.
                        5. Add Tags — Click tag buttons for narrative tags like Mobile or Spaceworthy.
                        6. Apply to HQ — Hit the Apply button to add everything to your headquarters. You can re-apply to update — it won't duplicate.
                        Build a starship as a mobile headquarters. Pick the team's average rank and the book's Starship Size table fills in Size, Health, and Passengers automatically (Secret Wars p.183). Then quick-add starship traits and tags, and apply them to the headquarters above.

                        🚗 Vehicles

                        🎓 How to Add Vehicles
                        1. Browse the buttons — Basic Vehicles are everyday rides (Car, Helicopter, etc.). Special Vehicles are signature rides from the books (Blackbird, Spider-Mobile, etc.). Each button shows Speed, Health, and passengers.
                        2. Click to add — Tap any button to add that vehicle to your HQ. It appears in the list below with all its stats filled in.
                        3. Or go custom — Open ➕ Custom Vehicle below the quick-add buttons, type a name and hit + Add Custom to create your own, then edit its stats in the card.
                        4. Edit in the card — Each vehicle card lets you change its name, Speed, Health, Size, Mode, and more. The colored bar shows its status (green = fine, red = destroyed).
                        5. Save to Garage Vault — Hit the 💾 button on any vehicle to save it to the cross-HQ Garage Vault, so you can reuse it on other headquarters.
                        Vehicles use the pilot's Melee/Agility defense (or TN 10 if unpiloted). Below half Health, speed is halved; below 1 Health, it stops working; at −Max Health, it's destroyed.
